historical_anchor: Historical 12 Jun TF58 shifted from the opening fighter sweep toward repeated bombing/airfield/defense suppression over the Marianas; relatively few Japanese aircraft rose to contest the raids.
Historical carrier aircraft also attacked the Saipan evacuation convoy over 11-12 Jun and inflicted very heavy merchant/escort losses.

branch_execution.event: Repeated fighter-bomber and bomber strikes against Saipan/Tinian airfields, radar/plot sites, fuel/ammunition handling, and known gun positions. One task-group effort remains weighted toward Guam/Rota.
Convoy/shipping searches exploit reports from 11 Jun. Dispersed packets are attacked when found; US aircraft spend more search time than in the dense historical convoy geometry.
Airfield reattack prevents comfortable runway repair cycles but does not fully close every strip before night.

major_US_ship_damage: NONE on 12 Jun; no coordinated Japanese anti-carrier strike reaches TF58.
operational_result: US local air superiority deepens and Japanese runway/C2 capacity is further degraded. FORAGER schedule remains intact; TF58 does not need to alter task-group geometry because of Japanese land-air action on 12 Jun.
